info.description: REST API of the Dulo family tree server.
info.title: Dulo API

tags.description: Administration of the roles and their permissions. Needs the administration feature with the matching access. Only the root user may change the built-in roles, and nobody may delete them.
tags.name: Roles

tags.description: The audit history: every change to every record, with the values before and after. Needs view access to the audit-log feature; changes to the tree settings, roles and users also need view access to administration.
tags.name: Audit

tags.description: Administration of the users: approve, disable, assign roles. Needs the administration feature: view to read, edit to change.
tags.name: Users

tags.description: The one-time initial setup. Until it's done, the rest of the API answers 503. The setup token is in the server log, or in dulo.setup.token.
tags.name: Setup

tags.description: The family tree of this server
tags.name: Tree

parameters.name: entityType

parameters.description: Only changes to the record with this id. Combine it with `entityType`: role keys are ids too.
parameters.name: entityId

parameters.description: Only changes by the user with this id.
parameters.name: actor

parameters.description: Only changes at or after this time (ISO 8601).
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: The `next` cursor of the previous page; leave it out for the first page.
parameters.name: after

400.description: An unknown entity type, an invalid cursor, limit or time range. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:validation`.

403.description: The caller may not view the audit log, or filters by an administrative type without administration access. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:forbidden`, `urn:dulo:problem:feature-disabled`, or says why the account is not active.

get.description: Public, for the sign-in page. Sorted by id. When an authorization request names one with the `idp` parameter, or only one is configured, the server skips the sign-in page and goes straight to it.
Returns the user, their roles and what they may do. Also works while the account waits for approval or is disabled, so clients can say why.

401.description: No valid access token. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:unauthorized`.

post.description: Creates the tree and the roles, and makes the signed-in caller the root user, who may do everything. Works once.

parameters.description: The one-time setup token. The server logs it on start, unless it is set in dulo.setup.token.
parameters.name: X-Dulo-Setup-Token

201.description: The new tree. Its address is in Location.

400.description: Invalid request, e.g. an unknown feature or a role a provider maps to but the request doesn't define. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:validation`.

401.description: No valid access token. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:unauthorized`.

403.description: Missing or wrong setup token. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:invalid-setup-token`.

409.description: The setup is done. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:setup-completed`.

409.description: The setup is done. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:setup-completed`.

get.summary: Get what the setup starts from

get.description: Returns the tree's name, description and the state of each feature. Every active user may read it.

401.description: No valid access token. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:unauthorized`.

403.description: The account is not active. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:account-pending` or `urn:dulo:problem:account-disabled`.

404.description: The initial setup is not done yet. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:tree-not-initialized`.

503.description: The initial setup isn't done yet. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:setup-required`.

patch.description: Changes the name, the description or the enabled features. Needs edit access to the administration feature. Left-out values stay as they are.

parameters.description: The ETag of the resource as last read. A change to an outdated copy fails with 412.
parameters.name: If-Match

400.description: Invalid change, e.g. an unknown feature or an empty name. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:validation`.

403.description: The caller may not change the tree. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:forbidden`, or says why the account is not active.

412.description: The tree changed since it was read. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:concurrent-modification`.

428.description: If-Match is missing. The problem type is `urn:dulo:problem:precondition-required`.

claimRoles.description: Roles mapped from the provider's claims at the last sign-in.

provider.description: The identity provider the user signs in with.

root.description: True for the user who did the initial setup.

version.description: Also the ETag; send it in If-Match to change the user.

actor.description: The id of the user who made the change.

changes.description: The fields the change affected. A creation lists every field with a value, a deletion every field as it was.

correlationId.description: Shared by the changes of one action.

entityId.description: The record's id; for roles, the role key.

entityVersion.description: The record's version after the change; for a deletion, its last version.

removedLinks.description: For a deletion: the references to the record it removed.

access.description: Allowed access: view, create, edit, delete.

after.description: The value after; null when the field has none or the record was deleted.

before.description: The value before; null when the field had none or the record didn't exist.

signInPath.description: Path that starts the sign-in with this provider. Open it in the browser during an authorization request.

Link.description: A reference from one record to another.

entityId.description: The id of the record that holds the reference.

entityType.description: The type of the record that holds the reference.

field.description: The field of that record that holds the reference.

permissions.description: What the user may do right now, per enabled feature. Empty while the account is not active.

roles.description: Role keys, from the identity provider's claims and assigned by hand.

root.description: True for the user who did the initial setup.

next.description: Opaque cursor of the next page: pass it as `after`. Null on the last page.

permissions.description: Replaces all of the role's permissions.

builtIn.description: Admin, editor, contributor and viewer are built in.

version.description: Also the ETag; send it in If-Match to change the role.

configuration.description: The merged configuration as YAML, with secrets masked and the source of each value as a comment.

features.description: The features that can be switched. Locked features are forced by the configuration.

identityProviders.description: The identity providers and how their claims map to roles. They come from the configuration and can't be changed here.

registrationMode.description: Whether new users are active right away (`auto`) or wait for approval (`approval`).

roles.description: The built-in roles with their default permissions.

defaultRole.description: The role of users whose claims match no mapping.

roleMappings.description: Claim value to the role keys it grants.

enabledFeatures.description: Keys of the features to switch on. Features the configuration forces keep their forced state.

roles.description: Roles to create or change. Built-in roles that are left out get their default permissions. Every role an identity provider maps to must exist.

pending.description: True until the initial setup is done. Until then the rest of the API answers 503.

description.description: At most 2000 characters. An empty string removes it.

enabledFeatures.description: Keys of the features to switch on, replacing the current ones. Features the configuration forces keep their forced state.

manualRoles.description: Role keys, replacing the roles an administrator assigned.

status.description: `active` approves a pending user or reactivates a disabled one.

oauth2.description: Dulo's own access tokens. Clients use the authorization code flow with PKCE; users sign in through one of the identity providers listed at /api/v1/identity-providers.
